title: Listening Practice: Joining a Cookery Course

sections.instructions: Questions 1-6: complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Questions 7-10: choose the correct answer.

transcript: NARRATOR: You will hear a man phoning a cookery school to enrol on a course. First, look at questions 1 to 6.
AGENT: Hello, Riverside Cookery School. This is Grace.
CALLER: Hi, Grace. I saw your advert for weekend courses and I'd like to sign up for one.
AGENT: Great. Which course were you interested in?
CALLER: I was looking at the bread-making one, but I think I'd get more out of the Italian course. Pasta and sauces.
AGENT: Italian it is. Can I take your full name?
CALLER: Sam Okafor. O, K, A, F, O, R.
AGENT: Thank you. And your email address?
CALLER: It's sam dot okafor at mailbox dot com.
AGENT: Got it. The Italian course runs on two dates this month: the ninth or the twenty-third.
CALLER: I'm away on the ninth, so the twenty-third, please.
AGENT: The twenty-third. The course starts at half past nine and finishes at about four. The full price is eighty-five pounds, but if you're a student it's sixty-five.
CALLER: I'm not a student any more, unfortunately, so the full price.
AGENT: No problem. Do you have any allergies we should know about?
CALLER: Yes, I'm allergic to nuts. Not dairy or anything else, just nuts.
AGENT: I'll make a note of that for the chef.
NARRATOR: Now look at questions 7 to 10.
CALLER: Is there anything I need to bring?
AGENT: We provide all the ingredients and equipment, and aprons. The only thing we ask is that you bring a container to take your food home in.
CALLER: Easy enough. How many people are usually in a group?
AGENT: We take a maximum of ten, but this one has eight booked so far, including you.
CALLER: And is lunch included?
AGENT: It is. You'll eat what you make in the morning session, so it's a working lunch.
CALLER: Perfect. Is there parking at the school?
AGENT: There's no car park, I'm afraid, and the street parking is only for residents. Most people come by train. The station is a five-minute walk.
CALLER: I'll take the train, then. Thanks for your help.

answer.rationale: He considered bread-making but chose the Italian course.
He is away on the ninth, so chooses the twenty-third.
'The course starts at half past nine.'
He is no longer a student, so he pays the full £85.

questions.prompt: What does Sam need to bring?

answer.rationale: Everything else is provided; bring a container to take food home.

questions.prompt: How many people have booked the course so far?

answer.rationale: The maximum is ten; eight are booked so far.

answer.rationale: There is no parking, so he will take the train.
